entries.note: Maya is an exceptional student. She finished the polynomial unit early and helped two classmates debug their factoring work without being asked. Consider recommending her for the math team.
Consistent high performance continues into Unit 2. Maya's midterm project outline is already submitted and shows real creative thinking — she's modeling loan amortization with quadratic curves.

Jaylen has real ability — when he's in class he participates well and grasps concepts quickly. The missing work from his absences is pulling his grade down significantly. I haven't been able to reach a parent yet. Will try again this week.

Spoke briefly with Jaylen after class. He mentioned things have been 'complicated at home' but didn't elaborate. I've flagged this to the counselor. He's bright enough to recover his grade if we can get him consistent attendance and help him make up his three missing assignments.

Ethan is working hard but the foundational gaps from Algebra I are showing. He stays after class occasionally and asks good questions. He would benefit from tutoring — I've suggested the peer tutoring program twice but he hasn't signed up yet.

Ethan's Unit 1 test score (49/100) is concerning. He understood the material in our one-on-one review but struggles with timed test conditions. Worth exploring whether there's a testing accommodation that might help.
Small but encouraging progress on homework completion rate this month. He got a 63 on HW04, his best homework score so far. The effort is there — he just needs more support to consolidate it.

Sofia is the strongest student in the class by a clear margin. Perfect attendance, every assignment on time, and she frequently finishes assessments well before the period ends. I've given her extension problems to keep her challenged.
Sofia's midterm project is outstanding — she's going beyond the rubric requirements. She asked if she could present it to the class. I said yes. This is a student to watch.

Marcus is clearly capable — his in-class work is strong when he's focused. However, he tends to socialize and gets off-task easily, which is reflected in uneven homework scores. Had a brief chat with him about it; he was receptive.

Marcus's tardiness is becoming a pattern. He's missing the first 5-10 minutes of instruction, which is when I introduce new concepts. His quiz scores have dipped on the chapters where this was most frequent.
Improvement this month — fewer tardies and his Q03 score was better. He seems more settled. I think a parent check-in would reinforce this positive momentum while it's happening.

Aaliyah tries hard when she's in class but the absences are creating compounding gaps. She missed the day I introduced rational expressions and hasn't fully caught up. I offered to email her class notes but she hasn't responded.

Aaliyah's cumulative grade is sitting near a D. I'm genuinely worried about her. She seems stressed and has mentioned once that she 'has a lot going on.' I'd like to set up a three-way conversation with a parent and the counselor before the end of the semester.

Noah is a strong student and a natural leader in group work. One thing to watch: he can dominate discussions in a way that shuts down quieter students. I've spoken to him about it gently and he's been more mindful.
Continued strong performance. The college visit absence in November is noted — he submitted the Unit 2 makeup quiz and scored an 87. Shows good initiative and responsibility.

Grace's attendance is the biggest concern in this class. She's missed 5 days already in September and several more tardies. When she is present she's quiet but attentive. I don't yet know what's driving the absences.

I've flagged Grace to the attendance office. Her grade is at risk of failure. She turned in HW04 and did reasonably on it (60/100), which tells me she's capable — but she needs to be here. This situation requires family involvement urgently.

Grace submitted her midterm project and it showed genuine understanding of the material. I gave her a 58 after applying the late penalty, but the underlying work was closer to a 70. She has capability; the attendance pattern is what's holding her back.

Diego is steady, reliable, and pleasant to have in class. He doesn't always participate verbally but his written work is consistently strong. I noticed he's been helping Ethan (S03) informally during group work — that's a nice dynamic.
Diego made up the work he missed during his family obligation absence without any prompting from me. His midterm project is on track. A solid, dependable student.

Priya is academically strong but has a tendency to challenge grading decisions in a way that can become disruptive. After Q01 she disputed two questions publicly during class. I spoke with her privately; she was more receptive one-on-one. I'll direct future grade questions to office hours.
Priya's performance has been excellent this unit. She seems to have channeled her competitive energy productively — she's formed a study group with two other students. The dynamic has been positive.
Priya's midterm project is one of the most polished in the class. Her study group is clearly working well. I'm glad to see her leadership instincts being applied collaboratively.
